issues.detail: 'customer_id' takes 3000 distinct values across the 3075 rows it is filled on. Left in the feature set a model can memorise it, which scores well in validation and predicts nothing on new rows.
issues.title: 'customer_id' looks like an identifier

issues.detail: 'email' takes 1946 distinct values across the 1995 rows it is filled on. Left in the feature set a model can memorise it, which scores well in validation and predicts nothing on new rows.
issues.title: 'email' looks like an identifier

issues.detail: 1727 of 3075 rows have no value for 'cancellation_reason'. Rows will be dropped or imputed by most models, and at this share that changes what the model learns.
issues.title: 56% of rows missing in 'cancellation_reason'

issues.detail: 1080 of 3075 rows have no value for 'email'. Rows will be dropped or imputed by most models, and at this share that changes what the model learns.
issues.title: 35% of rows missing in 'email'

issues.detail: ' Premium ', 'PREMIUM', 'Premium', 'premium' are the same value written differently, and every model will treat them as separate categories. 91 rows use a non-canonical spelling.
issues.title: 'plan' has 1 value spelled more than one way

issues.detail: 90 cells in 'discount_pct' hold a word meaning no value rather than a value. Left in place the column will not load as numeric, and every tool downstream treats them differently. Blanking them makes the gap explicit.
issues.title: 'discount_pct' writes missing values as 'none', 'N/A', 'unknown'

issues.detail: 90 of 3067 filled cells in 'discount_pct' are not numbers, the rest are. The non-numeric values are 'fifteen', 'ten', 'twenty'. Mixed types like this silently become a categorical column.
issues.title: 'discount_pct' mixes numbers and text

issues.detail: 60 rows fall into 30 groups of identical records, 30 of them redundant. Duplicates weight those records more heavily during training and inflate any score computed over them.
issues.title: 60 rows are exact duplicates

issues.detail: 20 pairs of rows agree on every field but one, covering 40 rows. Most commonly 'tenure_months' differs slightly. Near-copies usually come from a re-import or a partial edit, and they weight the same record twice.
issues.title: 20 near-duplicate row pairs

issues.detail: 12 rows sit far outside the rest of 'tenure_months'. The most extreme is 6900 against a median of 37. Measured against median absolute deviation, so a few large values cannot inflate the threshold and hide inside it.
issues.title: 12 outlying values in 'tenure_months'

issues.detail: 10 rows carry a 'signup_date' later than today, the latest being 2031-04-02. Usually a placeholder or a parsing slip rather than a real date.
issues.title: 10 dates in 'signup_date' are in the future

issues.detail: 8 rows have no value in over half their columns. Rows this thin usually come from a broken import rather than genuine gaps.
issues.title: 8 rows are more than half empty

issues.detail: Every row reads 'EU'. A column with no variation cannot carry information and only adds width to the model.
issues.title: 'region' has the same value in every row

issues.detail: The two correlate at 1.000. One of them is a restatement of the other, so keeping both adds width without adding signal.
issues.title: 'monthly_charges' and 'monthly_charges_eur' carry the same information

issues.detail: 255 of 3075 rows have no value for 'contract'. Worth knowing before you impute.
issues.title: 8.3% of rows missing in 'contract'

issues.detail: Padding appears in 1 columns, most of it in 'plan'. Whitespace is invisible on screen and still breaks a join, a grouping or a numeric cast.
issues.title: 30 cells have space around them

issues.detail: 'Enterprise' appear 3 times or so. Categories this thin cannot be learned and will not survive a split.
issues.title: 'plan' has 1 category with under 5 rows
